ayahs.1: I swear by this city—Makkah, the sacred sanctuary—
ayahs.2: Though you, O Prophet, are permitted to live in it while others would be barred from violating what is holy—yet even here you faced abuse.
ayahs.3: And by every parent and what they bear—the bond of lineage and responsibility Allah wove into human life.
ayahs.4: We created humankind in unceasing struggle—kabad: toil, pain, and uphill effort from birth through livelihood.
ayahs.5: Do they think no one has power over them?
ayahs.6: Boasting, "I have squandered enormous wealth!"—as if reckless spending were proof of freedom.
ayahs.7: Do they think no one sees?
ayahs.8: Have We not given them two eyes—
ayahs.10: And shown them the two paths—the clear ways of right and wrong?
ayahs.11: If only they had climbed the steep path—
ayahs.12: And what will explain to you what the steep path is?
ayahs.13: These opening letters—known as the muqatta'at—are among the signs whose full meaning Allah kept with Himself. They open the surah by reminding the reader that this Book is from beyond human authorship: approach it with humility, not arrogance.
ayahs.14: Or feeding, on a day of famine,
ayahs.16: Or a destitute person in the dust,
ayahs.17: Then, beyond that, being among those with iman—faith that reshapes how you live—who counsel one another to sabr, steadfast endurance, and to mercy.
ayahs.18: Those are the people of the right—the blessed companions.
ayahs.19: As for those who reject Our signs, they are the people of the left.
ayahs.20: Over them the Fire will close, sealed shut.
